node.title: Re: Why a regex *really* isn't good enough for HTML, even for "simple" tasks
node.author: Corion
node.doctext:
Here's the solution using plain [mod://WWW::Mechanize]. It fails the XHTML test, because (I think) it uses [mod://HTML::TokeParser], and somehow misparses the Six link:

#!/usr/bin/env perl use warnings; use strict; my $file = shift or die; print "##### WWW::Mechanize on $file #####\n"; my $html = do { open my $fh, '<', $file or die "$file: $!"; local $/; <$fh> }; use WWW::Mechanize; my $mech = WWW::Mechanize->new(); $mech->update_html($html); my @links = $mech->links(); for my $link (@links) { print $link->url, "\t", $link->text, "\n"; }

Since HTML::TokeParser and [mod://HTML::Parser] even live in the same distribution, I'll look at a pull request to change the parser type to the one that works.

Update: [https://github.com/libwww-perl/WWW-Mechanize/pull/298|The pull request]
